$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}A$.  The top normal stress

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$ gives
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$, i.e.

$A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and gives
$B=A\big[kh\tanh kh-1\big]/h$.
Then

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}= -2kA\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]/
\big[h\cosh kh\big]$,

so that

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$

is

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{kh\cosh kh}$,

i.e. with $\alpha=kh$

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}

\equiv\chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,

$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$.

Writing the restoring traction on the top as $\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the density ratio is made explicit,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
      =\chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$.

With the usual geodynamic identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the
normal stress balance

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big/\big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]$,
$\alpha=kh$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $kh\simeq1.2$.
In the lubrication long wave limit

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\simeq kh$,

the familiar viscous dynamic topography $e_{s}\propto kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with exponential screening for $kh\gg1$.

The $\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\alpha/[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]
=\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha/[1+\alpha\tanh\alpha]$, i.e. the
$kh\,{\rm sech}kh$ screened form, is the same kernel up to the
conventional $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base normalisation
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$ and the $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$
book keeping.  To $O(\alpha)$ it coincides with $\chi_{0}$,
$\chi_{0}=\chi_{\rm imp}+O(\alpha^{3})$, and both give the correct
thin-sheet $e_{s}\sim khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling.

The $\sinh$-numerator $\chi_{s}= \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+
\alpha^{2}]$ obtained by Colleagues 4,6 is the parity reversed sign
convention $\sigma_{xz}=+\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]$ and/or
$\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu W'$, which gives the unphysical
$\chi_{s}\sim\alpha^{2}$ thin-plate scaling and is ruled out by the
required $e_{s}\propto kh$ long-wave limit.  The remaining $O(1)$
differences are the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio and the
$1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base stress normalisation quoted in the literature.
reflection_text.3:
The harmonic Stokes problem is
$u_{x}=\Psi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Psi\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Psi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Psi'''-3k^{2}\Psi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Psi'''-k^{2}\Psi']\cos kx$.

With the steady free surface $u_{z}=0$, $u_{x}=0$
$\Psi(0)=\Psi'(0)=0$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Psi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Psi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.
The regular solution with $\Psi(0)=\Psi'(0)=0$ is

$\Psi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+bz\sinh kz$,

$\Psi'''(0)=-2ak^{3}$, $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Psi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Psi'(h)$ whence

$b=a\bigl(k\tanh kh-1/h\bigr)=a\,(kh\tanh kh-1)/h$.

Then

$\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi\big|_{h}=2k^{2}C\bigl[-a\xi+c(1+\xi S/C)\bigr]$
with $\xi=kh$, $C=\cosh\xi$, $S=\sinh\xi$ and $c=b/k$.
Using $c=a(S/C-1/\xi)$ one gets

$\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi\big|_{h}= -2ak^{2}\,\frac{\xi^{2}+C^{2}}{\xi C}$,

so that

$\mu[\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,\frac{\xi^{2}+C^{2}}{\xi C}$.

Hence in the steady state with $\alpha=kh$

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$,
$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$.

Writing the restoring traction as $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}
=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the density ratio is made explicit,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
      =\chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$,
$\alpha=kh$.

With the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the
normal stress balance

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\alpha\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $kh\simeq1.2$.

In the geological long wave $kh\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\simeq kh$,

the familiar viscous dynamic topography. Up to the $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$
and the $1+kh\tanh kh$ base normalisation this is the screened form
$\chi_{\rm imp}(kh)=kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]=kh\,{\rm sech}kh/
[1+kh\tanh kh]$, which coincides with the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/
[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ kernel to $O(\alpha)$. The
$\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ kernel is the parity
artefact obtained with the opposite sign convention
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[U'-kW]=-\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]$ and gives
$\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$, incompatible with the required
thin-sheet $e_{s}\sim h\tau_{b}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling.

The remaining $O(1)$ ambiguity is the $2\mu$ convention and the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor. With $\rho=\Delta\rho$ the textbook long
wave quoted form is $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e.
$\chi\approx kh$, with exponential screening for $kh\gg1$. The
impermeable-base compact form $e_{s}=kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is the same physics up to the stated book-keeping. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The harmonic mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
so that with the steady free surface $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$,

and the regular solution of $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ satisfying the
top kinematics can be taken as

$\Phi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+b z\sinh kz$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3}$,
$a=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

Zero normal traction at the base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$b=a\,k\,\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{2\sinh\alpha+\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
 =2\mu k\Big[\,b(\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha)-a k\alpha\cosh\alpha\Big]
 =S_{0}$.

Elimination of $a,b$ gives the closed steady relation

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}+2\alpha\sinh\alpha\cosh\alpha}
     {2\sinh\alpha+\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,
 i.e. with the conventional $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$ book-keeping

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

so that in the $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
\equiv\chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,

$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$.

Writing the restoring traction on the top in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
     =\chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

and with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the
normal-stress balance

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$.

Hence

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $kh\simeq1.2$,

and in the geological long-wave, lubrication limit

$e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}$, $\chi\simeq kh$,

the familiar viscous dynamic topography screening.  Up to the
conventional $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ and $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$
base normalisation this is the screened kernel normally quoted as

$\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
       =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha}
       =\frac{kh\,{\rm sech}kh}{1+kh\tanh kh}$,

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which
coincides with $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$
to $O(\alpha)$ and gives the same thin-sheet law
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
screening for $kh\gg1$.  The $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+
\alpha^{2}]$ sinh-numerator form is the parity/sign artefact obtained
with $\sigma_{xz}= -\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]$ and gives $\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$
for $\alpha\ll1$ and is therefore inconsistent with the required
thin-sheet $e_{s}\sim h\tau_{b}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is unity if the top stress is written with
the buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$.  This is the steady shear-driven
dynamic topography for the stated $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta
\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$
conditions. ∎

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the round-3 discussion has essentially narrowed the physics to one live choice, and the sinh-numerator family is now dead on the thin-sheet scaling.  Everyone agrees we need $\chi\sim kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$, and that the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ kernel is $\sim\alpha^{2}$ at long wave and is therefore out.

The remaining disagreement is the $W(0)=0$ / $\Phi(0)=0$ kinematic imposition versus what is actually stated at the top.  The problem statement is explicit: at $z=0$

* $\sigma_{zz}= \rho g e\cos kx$,
* $u_{x}=0$,

and nothing is stated about $u_{z}$.  With $\psi=\Phi\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $W'(0)=0$.  The condition $W(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, i.e. $u_{z}(0)=0$, is the steady-state $\dot e=0$ condition, not an instantaneous kinematic boundary condition for the velocity field.  Imposing it as Colleagues 1,2,3,5 do forces the basis 
$\Phi=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+bz\sinh kz$ and gives the
$\chi_{0}= \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ kernel.

If we keep only the stated top conditions $W'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, and work with the $U,W,P_{1}$ variables $u_{x}=U\sin kx$, $u_{z}=W\cos kx$, $p=P_{1}\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-P_{1}+2\mu W'$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]=-\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]$, the regular solution with $W'(0)=0$ is

$$
W(z)=b\,z\cosh kz+\bigl(-b/k+dz\bigr)\sinh kz,\qquad 
P_{1}(z)=2\mu\bigl[b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\bigr].
$$

The stated top stress is $P_{1}(0)=2\mu b=-\Delta\rho g e$.  The stated base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the “neglect lithostatic, pressure only induced’’ reading this is

$$
P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h),\qquad -\mu k^{-1}\bigl[W''+k^{2}W\bigr]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. pressure elimination at the base.  $P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$ gives

$$
d=b\Bigl[\frac{\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}\Bigr]
  =\frac{b}{\alpha}-b\tanh\alpha ,\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

and with $b=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu$

$$
S_{0}= -\frac{2\mu b}{\alpha}\,
\frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     =\Delta\rho g e\,\frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha}.
$$

Hence the steady observable topography with the boundary conditions actually written down is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
      =\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$$
\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
      =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh .
$$

That is $\chi_{\rm imp}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rm imp}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the long-wave lubrication limit and the familiar $kh\,{\rm sech}kh$ screening for finite $kh$.  In the $\rho$ normalisation used in the statement this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm imp}S_{0}/\rho g$, and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the normal stress balance it is the textbook viscous sheet dynamic topography.

The $\chi_{0}= \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ form obtained by Colleagues 1-3-5 is the same Stokes solution written with the extra kinematic restriction $\Phi(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$, and with the $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$ book-keeping kept in $\sigma_{zz}$.  In fact

$$
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
   =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha^{2}{\rm sech}^{2}\alpha}
   =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha}+O(\alpha^{3}),
$$

so the two kernels coincide to $O(\alpha)$ and share the same long-wave linear law and exponential screening.  The difference is precisely the $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base normalisation that comes from imposing $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as $P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$ with only $u_{x}(0)=0$ stated at the top, which is the condition quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,5 themselves as the conventional screened form $\chi_{\rm imp}= \alpha/[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]$.

With the stated BCs the physically faithful steady amplitude is therefore the impermeable-base kernel above, i.e. the familiar $e_{s}\simeq kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic topography, usually quoted in compact form

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{\rm imp}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rm imp}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}.
$$

This reproduces the required $\chi\sim kh$ thin-sheet limit, exponential screening at large $kh$, and matches the literature screening law that Colleagues 1,2,3,5 already cite as the standard $kh\,{\rm sech}kh$ form.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the disagreement can be traced to what is actually imposed kinematically at the free surface. The statement gives at $z=0$

* $\sigma_{zz}= \rho g e\cos kx$,
* $u_{x}=0$,

and no explicit $u_{z}(0)=0$. With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ the stated condition is
$\Phi'(0)=0$.  $\Phi(0)=0$, i.e. $W(0)=0$, is the steady-state
$ \dot e=0$ condition and is not an instantaneous kinematic condition
for the velocity field. Imposing $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ as done in the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ derivations is the
extra restriction that forces the $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ regular basis
and the $\cosh$ numerator.

It is cleaner to work with $u_{x}=U\sin kx$, $u_{z}=W\cos kx$,
$p=P_{1}\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$. Then

$\sigma_{zz}=-P_{1}+2\mu W'$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]
=-\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}W=0$,

and the regular solution with the stated $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $W'(0)=0$, is

$W(z)=b\,z\cosh kz+(-b/k+dz)\sinh kz$,

$P_{1}(z)=2\mu\big[b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big]$.

The top normal stress is $P_{1}(0)=2\mu b$, so with the restoring
traction written in the conventional buoyancy form
$\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$2\mu b=-\Delta\rho g e$,

and $W(0)=0$ is recovered in the steady limit. The stated base
conditions are

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

$P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$ gives

$b\cosh\alpha+d\sinh\alpha
=b\alpha\sinh\alpha+d\alpha\cosh\alpha$,

$\alpha=kh$, i.e.

$d=b\;\frac{\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
   =\frac{b}{\alpha}-b\tanh\alpha$.

Now

$W''+k^{2}W=2k\Big[bz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]$

so that

$-\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]_{h}
=-2\mu\Big[b\cosh\alpha+\alpha d\cosh\alpha
        +\alpha b\sinh\alpha\Big]$.

Eliminating $d$ with $b=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu$,

$S_{0}= -\frac{2\mu b}{\alpha}
       \frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     =\Delta\rho g e\,\frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha}$.

Hence in the steady state

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}\frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha}=S_{0}$,

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
     =\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
 =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha}$,
$\alpha=kh$.

In particular

$\chi_{\rm imp}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}^{\max}\approx0.42$ near $kh\approx1.2$,

so that the familiar long-wave viscous dynamic topography

$e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$,

and the exponential screening $e_{s}\propto kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\gg1$ is recovered. With the normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ used in the statement this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm imp}S_{0}/\rho g$, and with the usual geodynamic identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the normal stress balance it is the textbook $kh\,{\rm sech}kh$ kernel.

The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ form obtained with the additional $\Phi(0)=0$ i.e. $W(0)=0$ kinematic condition is the same Stokes solution written with the pressure eliminated as $\sigma_{zz}=(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']$ and with the $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$ book-keeping. Up to the conventional $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base normalisation it coincides with $\chi_{\rm imp}$, and both give the required $kh$ linear law and exponential screening. The compact physically observable form with the boundary conditions as stated, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, is the impermeable-base kernel above, conventionally quoted as $e_{s}\approx kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. The $\sinh$-numerator $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ is ruled out by the $kh\ll1$ lubrication scaling $\chi\sim\alpha$, which the expression above satisfies.

5.text:
With the harmonic mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$$
(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx,
\qquad 
p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx,
$$

the regular solution with a flat steady free surface is

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Bz\sinh kz  ,
$$

so that

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}A=\rho g e
\cos kx ,
$$

i.e.

$$
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}\; .
$$

The zero normal traction at the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,

$$
B=A\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}
   =A\,\frac{\alpha\tanh\alpha-1}{h},\qquad 
\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

and with

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-Ak^{2}z\cosh kz
      +B\cosh kz+Bkz\sinh kz\Big]
$$

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kA}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Hence

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kA}{h\cosh\alpha}
        \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]
     =\rho ge\,\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
     =S_{0} ,
$$

in the steady state $\dot e=0$.  With $\alpha=kh$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     \equiv \chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g} ,
$$

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

is the Stokes steady amplitude for the normalisation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $u_{x}(0)=0$.
Writing the restoring traction on the top in the usual buoyancy form
$\sigma_{zz}^{\,{\rm top}}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}\,
       \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
     =\chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad 
\alpha=kh,
$$

and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the
normal stress balance

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad \alpha=kh,
$$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\alpha\gg1,
$$

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $kh\simeq1.2$.  In the lubrication long-wave
limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh\;\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho},
$$

i.e. with $\rho=\Delta\rho$ the familiar viscous dynamic topography

In the 2-D Stokes problem put

\begin{equation*}
\psi (x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
so that $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0$ and with the $2\mu\varepsilon_{ij}$ 
convention

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$.
On the flat steady free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$ and the
steady state $\dot e=0$ is $\Phi(0)=0$.  With

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(z)=a\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+bz\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu k a
               =\rho g e\cos kx ,
\qquad a=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\end{equation*}
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and gives

\begin{equation*}
b=a\,\frac{kh\tanh kh-1}{h},
\qquad \alpha\equiv kh .
\end{equation*}
Hence

\begin{equation*}
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big|_{h}
      =-\frac{2ka}{h\cosh\alpha}
        \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] ,
\end{equation*}
and with $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$

\begin{equation*}
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =\rho g e\,
       \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}\;,
\end{equation*}
i.e. in the steady state

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}=\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
      \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad \alpha=kh,
\end{equation*}
so that with the normal stress written in the buoyancy form
$\sigma_{zz}^{{\rm top}}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
       \,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
     =\chi(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad 
\alpha=kh ,
\end{equation*}
which with the usual geodynamic identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
in the normal stress balance is

\[
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad 
e_{s}=\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$\chi_{0}(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$,
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $kh\simeq1.2$.  In particular

\[
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}\,S_{0}\,
\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho},\qquad kh\ll1,
\]

and with $\rho=\Delta\rho$ the familiar viscous dynamic topography

\[
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh,
\]

with exponential screening for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional
$2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$ and $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base
normalisation this is the impermeable–base screened kernel

\[
\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=
\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
=\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha},
\qquad e_{s}\simeq 
\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha}
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

$\chi_{\rm imp}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\chi_{\rm imp}\sim\alpha
e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$, and
$\chi_{\rm imp}= \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]+O(\alpha^{3})$.
With the usual $\rho=\Delta\rho$ normalisation this is the textbook
$ e_{s}\approx kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous sheet
response, $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the long wave
$kh\ll1$ limit, i.e. the $kh\,{\rm sech}kh$ screening law quoted in the
literature.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is unity when the top
stress is written with the buoyancy density $\Delta\rho$. ∎

public_text.4:
I think the round-3 discussion has essentially narrowed the physics to one live choice, and the sinh-numerator family is now dead on the thin-sheet scaling.  Everyone agrees we need $\chi\sim kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$, and that the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ kernel is $\sim\alpha^{2}$ at long wave and is therefore out.

The remaining disagreement is the $W(0)=0$ / $\Phi(0)=0$ kinematic imposition versus what is actually stated at the top.  The problem statement is explicit: at $z=0$

* $\sigma_{zz}= \rho g e\cos kx$,
* $u_{x}=0$,

and nothing is stated about $u_{z}$.  With $\psi=\Phi\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $W'(0)=0$.  The condition $W(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, i.e. $u_{z}(0)=0$, is the steady-state $\dot e=0$ condition, not an instantaneous kinematic boundary condition for the velocity field.  Imposing it as Colleagues 1,2,3,5 do forces the basis 
$\Phi=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+bz\sinh kz$ and gives the
$\chi_{0}= \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ kernel.

If we keep only the stated top conditions $W'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, and work with the $U,W,P_{1}$ variables $u_{x}=U\sin kx$, $u_{z}=W\cos kx$, $p=P_{1}\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-P_{1}+2\mu W'$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]=-\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]$, the regular solution with $W'(0)=0$ is

$$
W(z)=b\,z\cosh kz+\bigl(-b/k+dz\bigr)\sinh kz,\qquad 
P_{1}(z)=2\mu\bigl[b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\bigr].
$$

The stated top stress is $P_{1}(0)=2\mu b=-\Delta\rho g e$.  The stated base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the “neglect lithostatic, pressure only induced’’ reading this is

$$
P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h),\qquad -\mu k^{-1}\bigl[W''+k^{2}W\bigr]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. pressure elimination at the base.  $P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$ gives

$$
d=b\Bigl[\frac{\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}\Bigr]
  =\frac{b}{\alpha}-b\tanh\alpha ,\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

and with $b=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu$

$$
S_{0}= -\frac{2\mu b}{\alpha}\,
\frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     =\Delta\rho g e\,\frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha}.
$$

Hence the steady observable topography with the boundary conditions actually written down is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
      =\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$$
\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
      =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh .
$$

That is $\chi_{\rm imp}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rm imp}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the long-wave lubrication limit and the familiar $kh\,{\rm sech}kh$ screening for finite $kh$.  In the $\rho$ normalisation used in the statement this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm imp}S_{0}/\rho g$, and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the normal stress balance it is the textbook viscous sheet dynamic topography.

The $\chi_{0}= \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ form obtained by Colleagues 1-3-5 is the same Stokes solution written with the extra kinematic restriction $\Phi(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$, and with the $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$ book-keeping kept in $\sigma_{zz}$.  In fact

$$
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
   =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha^{2}{\rm sech}^{2}\alpha}
   =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha}+O(\alpha^{3}),
$$

so the two kernels coincide to $O(\alpha)$ and share the same long-wave linear law and exponential screening.  The difference is precisely the $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base normalisation that comes from imposing $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as $P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$ with only $u_{x}(0)=0$ stated at the top, which is the condition quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,5 themselves as the conventional screened form $\chi_{\rm imp}= \alpha/[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]$.

With the stated BCs the physically faithful steady amplitude is therefore the impermeable-base kernel above, i.e. the familiar $e_{s}\simeq kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic topography, usually quoted in compact form

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{\rm imp}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rm imp}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}.
$$

This reproduces the required $\chi\sim kh$ thin-sheet limit, exponential screening at large $kh$, and matches the literature screening law that Colleagues 1,2,3,5 already cite as the standard $kh\,{\rm sech}kh$ form.

I think the disagreement can be traced to what is actually imposed kinematically at the free surface. The statement gives at $z=0$

* $\sigma_{zz}= \rho g e\cos kx$,
* $u_{x}=0$,

and no explicit $u_{z}(0)=0$. With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ the stated condition is
$\Phi'(0)=0$.  $\Phi(0)=0$, i.e. $W(0)=0$, is the steady-state
$ \dot e=0$ condition and is not an instantaneous kinematic condition
for the velocity field. Imposing $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ as done in the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ derivations is the
extra restriction that forces the $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ regular basis
and the $\cosh$ numerator.

It is cleaner to work with $u_{x}=U\sin kx$, $u_{z}=W\cos kx$,
$p=P_{1}\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$. Then

$\sigma_{zz}=-P_{1}+2\mu W'$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]
=-\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}W=0$,

and the regular solution with the stated $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $W'(0)=0$, is

$W(z)=b\,z\cosh kz+(-b/k+dz)\sinh kz$,

$P_{1}(z)=2\mu\big[b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big]$.

The top normal stress is $P_{1}(0)=2\mu b$, so with the restoring
traction written in the conventional buoyancy form
$\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$2\mu b=-\Delta\rho g e$,

and $W(0)=0$ is recovered in the steady limit. The stated base
conditions are

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

$P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$ gives

$b\cosh\alpha+d\sinh\alpha
=b\alpha\sinh\alpha+d\alpha\cosh\alpha$,

$\alpha=kh$, i.e.

$d=b\;\frac{\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
   =\frac{b}{\alpha}-b\tanh\alpha$.

Now

$W''+k^{2}W=2k\Big[bz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]$

so that

$-\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]_{h}
=-2\mu\Big[b\cosh\alpha+\alpha d\cosh\alpha
        +\alpha b\sinh\alpha\Big]$.

Eliminating $d$ with $b=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu$,

$S_{0}= -\frac{2\mu b}{\alpha}
       \frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     =\Delta\rho g e\,\frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha}$.

Hence in the steady state

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}\frac{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha}=S_{0}$,

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
     =\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha}
 =\frac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha}$,
$\alpha=kh$.

In particular

$\chi_{\rm imp}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}^{\max}\approx0.42$ near $kh\approx1.2$,

so that the familiar long-wave viscous dynamic topography

$e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$,

and the exponential screening $e_{s}\propto kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\gg1$ is recovered. With the normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ used in the statement this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm imp}S_{0}/\rho g$, and with the usual geodynamic identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the normal stress balance it is the textbook $kh\,{\rm sech}kh$ kernel.

The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ form obtained with the additional $\Phi(0)=0$ i.e. $W(0)=0$ kinematic condition is the same Stokes solution written with the pressure eliminated as $\sigma_{zz}=(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']$ and with the $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$ book-keeping. Up to the conventional $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base normalisation it coincides with $\chi_{\rm imp}$, and both give the required $kh$ linear law and exponential screening. The compact physically observable form with the boundary conditions as stated, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, is the impermeable-base kernel above, conventionally quoted as $e_{s}\approx kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. The $\sinh$-numerator $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ is ruled out by the $kh\ll1$ lubrication scaling $\chi\sim\alpha$, which the expression above satisfies.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes sheet with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$. 
With the $2\mu\varepsilon_{ij}-p$ convention

$p=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu(\Phi''+k^2\Phi)\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

For a steady topography $\dot e=0$ the free surface can be taken flat in the steady limit. $u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$, and steady $\dot e=0$ is $\Phi(0)=0$. The regular branch with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is

$\Phi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+bz\sinh kz$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^3$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, 
so $a=-\rho ge/2\mu k^2$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives $b=a\,(kh\tanh kh-1)/h$.
With $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$,

$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ $\to$ $S_0=\rho ge\,[\alpha^2+\cosh^2\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$,
$\alpha=kh$.

Hence with $\sigma_{zz}^{top}=\rho ge\cos kx$

$e_s= S_0/ \rho g\; \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^2+\cosh^2\alpha]\equiv\chi_0(\alpha)S_0/\rho g$,

$\chi_0(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]$,
$\chi_0=\alpha+O(\alpha^3)$, $\chi_0\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $\alpha\simeq1.2$.

Writing the restoring stress with buoyancy contrast $\sigma_{zz}^{top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]\;S_0/\rho g
     =\chi(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]$, 
and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the normal balance $\chi=\chi_0$.

Long-wave lubrication: $\chi\simeq\alpha$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, exponential screening for $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}$.

Current round disagreement is the kinematic condition at the free surface. The statement gives only $u_x(0)=0$, i.e. $W'(0)=0$ in $u_x=U\sin kx$, $u_z=W\cos kx$, and does not state $u_z(0)=0$ as an instantaneous BC. Imposing $W(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$ as Colleagues 1,2,3,5 do gives $\chi_0$ above. Keeping only the stated $W'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ with the $U,W,P_1$ variables gives the regular solution $W=bz\cosh kz+(-b/k+dz)\sinh kz$, $P_1=2\mu[b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$, $2\mu b=-\Delta\rho g e$ and $P_1(h)=2\mu W'(h)$. This yields

$S_0=\Delta\rho g e\,[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]/\alpha$,

$e_s=\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\alpha/[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]
      =\alpha{\rm sech}\alpha/[1+\alpha\tanh\alpha]$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}=\alpha+O(\alpha^3)$, $\chi_{\rm imp}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

The two kernels coincide to $O(\alpha)$:
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]=\alpha{\rm sech}\alpha/[1+\alpha^2{\rm sech}^2\alpha]
 =\alpha{\rm sech}\alpha/[1+\alpha\tanh\alpha]+O(\alpha^3)$,
so the thin-sheet law and exponential screening are identical. The difference is the $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base normalisation and the $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$ book-keeping, i.e. the extra $\Phi(0)=0/W(0)=0$ steady condition.

The $\sinh$-numerator kernel $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]$, giving $\chi\sim\alpha^2$ for $\alpha\ll1$, is ruled out by the required $e_s\sim h\tau_b/\Delta\rho g$ scaling.

Unresolved $O(1)$ normalisation remains: $2\mu$ vs $\mu$ in $\sigma_{ij}$, the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor when the top stress is written with plate density $\rho$ but the amplitude is normalised by $\Delta\rho g$, and whether the steady $W(0)=0$ condition is to be imposed. Robust physical content is the linear long-wave scaling $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and exponential screening $e_s\propto kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\gg1$, conventionally quoted as $e_s\approx kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ or, with the $\Phi(0)=0$ steady basis, $e_s\approx\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

     =\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}\,
       \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

normal stress balance

$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]^{-1}$,
$e_{s}=\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{0}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi_{0}\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$,
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $kh\simeq1.2$.
In the geological lubrication limit

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\simeq kh$,

the familiar viscous dynamic topography with exponential screening for

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

With a steady flat free surface the stated $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the steady
$\dot e=0$ kinematic condition give $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
The regular branch can be taken as
$\Phi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+b z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3}$,
$a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives
$b=a\big[\alpha\tanh\alpha-1\big]/h$, $\alpha=kh$, and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
 =-\dfrac{2\mu k a}{h}\dfrac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\cosh\alpha}
 =\rho g e\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}=S_{0}$.

Hence in the $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
     \equiv\chi_{0}(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$,
$\alpha=kh$,
$\chi_{0}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi_{0}\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$,
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $kh\simeq1.2$.

Writing the restoring traction on the top in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}\,
       \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
     =\chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$,
and with the usual geodynamic identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the
normal stress balance

$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$,
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$, the familiar viscous
dynamic topography screening.  Up to the conventional $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$
and $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base normalisation this is the screened kernel
normally quoted as

$\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\alpha\big/[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]
 =\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha/[1+\alpha\tanh\alpha]$,
$e_{s}\simeq\chi_{\rm imp}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
which coincides with $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ to
$O(\alpha)$ and gives the same thin-sheet law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential screening $e_{s}\propto kh\,
e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\gg1$.

The disagreement in the current round is the kinematic imposition at the
free surface.  Imposing only the stated $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $W'(0)=0$, and
$P_{1}(h)=2\mu W'(h)$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, with

$S_{0}=\Delta\rho g e\,[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]/\alpha$, i.e.

\alpha\sinh\alpha]$.  This is the $W(0)=0$ kinematic-free form quoted by

law.  The $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$ sinh-numerator
kernel is the parity/sign artefact which gives $\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ for

$e_{s}\sim h\tau_{b}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is
unity when the top stress is written with the buoyancy contrast
$\Delta\rho$.  This is the steady shear-driven dynamic topography for
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

 =\dfrac{\alpha\,{\rm sech}\alpha}{1+\alpha\tanh\alpha}$,

The Stokes sheet with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$. 
With the $2\mu\varepsilon_{ij}-p$ convention

$p=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu(\Phi''+k^2\Phi)\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

For a steady topography $\dot e=0$ the free surface can be taken flat in the steady limit. $u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$, and steady $\dot e=0$ is $\Phi(0)=0$. The regular branch with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is

$\Phi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+bz\sinh kz$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^3$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, 
so $a=-\rho ge/2\mu k^2$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives $b=a\,(kh\tanh kh-1)/h$.
With $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$,

$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ $\to$ $S_0=\rho ge\,[\alpha^2+\cosh^2\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$,
$\alpha=kh$.

Hence with $\sigma_{zz}^{top}=\rho ge\cos kx$

$e_s= S_0/ \rho g\; \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^2+\cosh^2\alpha]\equiv\chi_0(\alpha)S_0/\rho g$,

$\chi_0(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]$,
$\chi_0=\alpha+O(\alpha^3)$, $\chi_0\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.48$ at $\alpha\simeq1.2$.

Writing the restoring stress with buoyancy contrast $\sigma_{zz}^{top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]\;S_0/\rho g
     =\chi(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]$, 
and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the normal balance $\chi=\chi_0$.

Long-wave lubrication: $\chi\simeq\alpha$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, exponential screening for $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}$.

Current round disagreement is the kinematic condition at the free surface. The statement gives only $u_x(0)=0$, i.e. $W'(0)=0$ in $u_x=U\sin kx$, $u_z=W\cos kx$, and does not state $u_z(0)=0$ as an instantaneous BC. Imposing $W(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$ as Colleagues 1,2,3,5 do gives $\chi_0$ above. Keeping only the stated $W'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ with the $U,W,P_1$ variables gives the regular solution $W=bz\cosh kz+(-b/k+dz)\sinh kz$, $P_1=2\mu[b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$, $2\mu b=-\Delta\rho g e$ and $P_1(h)=2\mu W'(h)$. This yields

$S_0=\Delta\rho g e\,[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]/\alpha$,

$e_s=\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}(\alpha)=\alpha/[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha]
      =\alpha{\rm sech}\alpha/[1+\alpha\tanh\alpha]$,

$\chi_{\rm imp}=\alpha+O(\alpha^3)$, $\chi_{\rm imp}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

The two kernels coincide to $O(\alpha)$:
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]=\alpha{\rm sech}\alpha/[1+\alpha^2{\rm sech}^2\alpha]
 =\alpha{\rm sech}\alpha/[1+\alpha\tanh\alpha]+O(\alpha^3)$,
so the thin-sheet law and exponential screening are identical. The difference is the $1+\alpha\tanh\alpha$ base normalisation and the $2\mu\leftrightarrow\mu$ book-keeping, i.e. the extra $\Phi(0)=0/W(0)=0$ steady condition.

The $\sinh$-numerator kernel $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]$, giving $\chi\sim\alpha^2$ for $\alpha\ll1$, is ruled out by the required $e_s\sim h\tau_b/\Delta\rho g$ scaling.

Unresolved $O(1)$ normalisation remains: $2\mu$ vs $\mu$ in $\sigma_{ij}$, the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor when the top stress is written with plate density $\rho$ but the amplitude is normalised by $\Delta\rho g$, and whether the steady $W(0)=0$ condition is to be imposed. Robust physical content is the linear long-wave scaling $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and exponential screening $e_s\propto kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\gg1$, conventionally quoted as $e_s\approx kh\,{\rm sech}kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ or, with the $\Phi(0)=0$ steady basis, $e_s\approx\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}\,
       \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
     =\chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$,
